A.summary:
This change adds an --agent flag to "sashiko review" and "sashiko-cli
local" so AI coding agents running local reviews get a compact,
non-interactive result. In agent mode the plain-text report and summary
LLM stages are skipped, the prompts and server submission are bypassed,
and stdout carries a concise JSON object. GEMINI.md now tells agents to
pass --agent.

Before:
  sashiko review --project sashiko HEAD~1..HEAD prints either the
  human-formatted report (--format text) or the full result JSON
  (--format json). The full JSON includes the LLM history, input_context,
  inline_review and dismissed concerns. The report and summary stages
  always run when there are findings. With a dirty worktree on a
  terminal, it asks "Do you want to proceed? [y/N]". sashiko-cli local
  submits to a running server if one is reachable, and with
  --interactive it pauses for a rebuttal after issues are found.

After:
  sashiko review --project sashiko --agent HEAD~1..HEAD skips the report
  and summary stages, never prompts about a dirty worktree, and prints
  one JSON object such as:
  {"status": "issues_found", "baseline": "abc1234", "patches": [...],
  "findings": [...], "concerns": [...], "tokens_in": 1200,
  "tokens_out": 300, "tokens_cached": 800}
  The status is "error" if the result carries an error, "issues_found"
  if there are findings, and otherwise "clean". The keys "partial" and
  "error" appear only when present in the result. History,
  input_context, inline_review and dismissed concerns are omitted. The
  --agent flag takes precedence over --format. sashiko-cli local --agent
  always runs the review locally instead of submitting to a server,
  forwards --agent to the worker, and does not enter the interactive
  re-run pause.

Internally, the flag is carried through ReviewOptions and WorkerOptions
into WorkerConfig.skip_report and the workflow state, where the Linux
report stage and the Sashiko report and summary stages use skip_if. The
worker leaves review_inline empty rather than "No issues found." when
the report is skipped, and drops "report" and "summary" from the planned
stage progress list. New tests cover the output formatter, CLI parsing
of the flag, and a worker run for both the Linux and Sashiko projects
that fails if a report or summary prompt is issued.
A.inline_review:
- [MEDIUM] In src/local_review.rs (format_agent_review_output), a result whose
  review is null is reported as status clean. run_worker_in_worktree returns
  early with review null and no error key when --no-ai is set or
  review_patch_index matches no patch, so an agent sees clean with empty
  findings although no patch was reviewed, and may open a PR as if
  self-review had passed. The only hint is tokens_in of 0. Emit a
  not_reviewed status (or an explicit reason field) when review is null or
  absent, and add a test for it.

- [MEDIUM] In src/local_review.rs (format_agent_review_output), status is
  issues_found whenever findings is non-empty, but the exit code is 1 only
  for new High or Critical findings (result_has_high_or_critical_findings in
  src/main.rs, and the severity counts in handle_local in
  src/bin/sashiko-cli.rs). A run with only pre-existing, Medium or Low
  findings prints issues_found and exits 0, so an agent told to resolve
  reported issues can loop on findings the CLI treats as success. Also,
  error is copied when non-null while result_has_error requires a non-empty
  string, and partial true does not affect status. Align status with the
  exit-code rule or document the split, and add a test for it.

- [MEDIUM] In src/main.rs (handle_review_command) and src/bin/sashiko-cli.rs
  (handle_local), failures that occur before a result exists bypass the
  agent JSON branch. A run_git_review error, empty worker output or
  unparsable worker output returns Err, so sashiko review prints nothing on
  stdout, and sashiko-cli prints a plain text Error line on stdout. Both
  exit 1, the same code used for new High or Critical findings. An agent
  loop cannot tell an infrastructure failure from findings and gets no JSON
  error object, despite the commit message promising error metadata. In
  agent mode emit a status error JSON object on stdout, keep diagnostics on
  stderr, and exit 3 as result_has_error does.

- [LOW] In src/bin/sashiko-cli.rs (handle_local), --agent silently overrides
  other flags: --interactive is ignored (interactive && !agent), --format
  text still prints JSON, and the running-server submit path is skipped.
  There is no clap conflict, no stderr note, and the flag help text mentions
  none of it. Declare conflicts_with or document the overrides in the help.

- [LOW] In src/worker/prompts.rs (Worker::run, ParallelResolved handler) and
  src/main.rs (handle_review_command), the new --agent wiring has no
  executing test. The new tests cover only clap parsing, the pure formatter,
  and a Worker run with no progress callback. The planned stage filter for
  report and summary, the dirty-worktree prompt bypass, the interactive
  guard, the server bypass and forwarding of --agent to the worker
  subprocess can all be reverted while every test stays green.

- [LOW] In src/bin/sashiko-cli.rs (handle_local), --agent skips the server
  queue and always runs a local worker subprocess, so the review semaphore
  and timeout_seconds kill in the server reviewer no longer apply, and the
  wait on the child (wait_with_output) has no wall-clock timeout. Parallel
  agent invocations multiply worktrees and model calls, and a stalled
  provider can block the agent loop indefinitely. The missing timeout is
  pre-existing for --force-local, but --agent makes it the default even when
  a server is running. Wrap the wait in a timeout with an explicit kill, or
  document the limit.

findings.explanation: Contained flag-hygiene defect. sashiko-cli local --interactive --agent accepts both flags but drops the rebuttal loop (interactive && !agent) with no stderr note and no clap conflicts_with. --format text --agent prints JSON. --agent also skips the running-server submit path (!force_local && !agent), so a review the daemon would have queued runs as a local subprocess. The commit message states the bypass, but the flag help text mentions none of these overrides. Impact is a surprised user or agent, with no data loss.

findings.problem: --agent reports status clean when no AI review ran
findings.explanation: Consequence: an agent reads status "clean" with empty findings although no patch was reviewed, and may open or update a PR as if self-review had passed. Reachability: in run_worker_in_worktree, options.no_ai clears patches_to_review, and a review_patch_index that matches no patch leaves it empty. Either way the early return emits {patchset_id, baseline, patches, review: null, input_context: "", tokens_in: 0, tokens_out: 0, tokens_cached: 0}. That object has no top-level error key and no skipped or not_reviewed marker, so result_has_error is false. format_agent_review_output then maps the missing review to an empty findings list with unwrap_or_default, and status falls through to "clean". Both callers pass the result through unchanged: main.rs handle_review_command calls format_agent_review_output(&result), and sashiko-cli handle_local calls it on the worker JSON. The only tell is tokens_in = 0, which a consumer has no reason to interpret as 'not reviewed'. The text path prints that no AI review was run, so agent mode loses a distinction the human path keeps. Severity is capped at Medium because the documented loop in GEMINI.md (sashiko review --project sashiko --agent <commit>) does not pass --no-ai or --review-patch-index, so a user has to add those flags or mistype an index. The new test has no review: null fixture, so it would not catch this. A fix is to emit status "not_reviewed" (or an explicit reason field) when review is null or absent, and add a test for it.

locations.code_snippet: let status = if result_has_error(result) { "error" } else if !findings.is_empty() { "issues_found" } else { "clean" };
locations.why_this_location_matters: There is no branch for a result whose review is null, so an unreviewed result is labelled clean.

Skipping AI review."); return Ok(json!({ "patchset_id": patchset_id, "baseline": baseline_arg, "patches": patch_results, "review": null, "input_context": "", "tokens_in": 0, "tokens_out": 0, "tokens_cached": 0 }));
locations.why_this_location_matters: The early return carries no error and no skipped marker, so a consumer cannot tell it from a clean review.

findings.problem: --agent status disagrees with exit code on preexisting/Low/Medium
findings.explanation: Consequence: in --agent mode the JSON status says issues_found for findings that do not fail the command, so an agent keyed on status and told by GEMINI.md to 'resolve any reported issues' can keep fixing or looping on findings the CLI treats as success. Reachability: every `sashiko review --agent` and `sashiko-cli local --agent` run. Verified code: format_agent_review_output sets status to 'error' if result_has_error, else 'issues_found' whenever `findings` is non-empty, with no look at `preexisting` or `severity`. The exit code uses a narrower rule. In main.rs, result_has_error exits 3, and result_has_high_or_critical_findings exits 1 only when `is_new && matches!(severity, critical|high)`. In sashiko-cli.rs, count_severities gives `counts.critical.new > 0 || counts.high.new > 0` for exit 1. So a result with only preexisting findings, or only new Medium/Low findings, prints status 'issues_found' and exits 0. I found no code or comment in the diff that documents this split (I did not search the docs or prompts beyond the diff). The findings keep their `preexisting` and `severity` fields, so an agent that reads them can tell the difference, but the headline `status` field cannot. The new test only covers a single High finding with no `preexisting` key, so it does not exercise this divergence. Secondary issue, same function: it copies `error` whenever it is non-null (`!err.is_null()`), but result_has_error requires a non-empty string. An empty-string or non-string `error` therefore gives status 'clean' or 'issues_found' alongside an `error` key. Likewise `partial: true` is copied but does not change `status`. I did not read the code that builds `error` in run_worker_in_worktree, so whether it can ever be empty or non-string is assumed; if it is always a non-empty string, only the status/exit mismatch stands. Capped at Medium because the status field is a new, undocumented contract and the full finding data is still present in the output.

locations.why_this_location_matters: Status is derived from non-empty findings only, ignoring preexisting and severity, and the error key is copied by a different test (non-null) than result_has_error (non-empty string).
The exit-code predicate (used by main.rs) counts only new High/Critical findings.
The local command uses the same narrow rule, so the exit code stays 0 while status says issues_found.

findings.problem: --agent failures before a result emit no JSON and exit 1
findings.explanation: Consequence: an agent loop that runs 'sashiko review --project sashiko --agent' (as GEMINI.md now instructs) or 'sashiko-cli local --agent' cannot tell an infrastructure failure from 'new High/Critical findings', and has no JSON error object to parse. Both cases exit 1, and the failure case emits no JSON. Reachability: any Err before a result Value exists, such as a run_git_review error, an empty worker stdout (worker crashed or was killed), or non-JSON worker stdout. Verified in code. (1) sashiko review: handle_review_command does 'let result = result?;' before the 'if agent' branch (src/main.rs ~2259), so format_agent_review_output never runs. main() is 'async fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>>', so the Err makes the process print the Debug-formatted error to stderr and exit 1. Stdout is empty. The findings path in the same function ends in std::process::exit(1) when result_has_high_or_critical_findings. Exit 1 is therefore shared, while result_has_error uses exit(3) only when a result exists. (2) sashiko-cli local: handle_local returns Err('Review subprocess produced no output (exit code: N)') or Err('Failed to parse review output JSON ...') before the 'if agent' print. main() then runs print_colored(Color::Red, 'Error: ') and println!('{}', e) to STDOUT, then std::process::exit(1). So stdout is not empty here but holds a non-JSON line 'Error: ...', which a JSON parser rejects, and again the exit code is 1, same as findings (exit(1) at count critical.new/high.new > 0). A diagnostic on stdout also breaks the machine-output-on-stdout, diagnostics-on-stderr rule. The commit message says the JSON carries 'any error or partial-completion metadata', but format_agent_review_output only reports error/partial when a result Value already exists; the Err paths above never reach it. The unit test only covers a result that already contains 'error', so it would not fail if these paths were broken. Only the worker's own error path (src/main.rs ~377, which prints an error JSON then exit(1)) yields a parseable result, and handle_local then maps it to exit 3. Not Critical/High: the failure is loud (non-zero exit plus stderr text) and the ambiguity requires a failure before any result exists. Fix: in agent mode, convert the Err into a {status:'error', error:...} JSON on stdout and exit with the same code as result_has_error (3), keeping diagnostics on stderr.

locations.why_this_location_matters: Early return on run_git_review Err happens before the agent JSON branch, so no JSON reaches stdout and main() exits 1 via the Result return.
Same exit code 1 is used for new High/Critical findings, so callers cannot distinguish findings from a failed review.
Empty or unparsable subprocess output returns Err before the agent branch prints format_agent_review_output.
After printing 'Error: ...' as plain text on stdout, any run_command Err exits 1, colliding with the findings exit code.

findings.problem: --agent skips server queue limits and wall-clock timeout
findings.explanation: Reachable only when an operator or agent runs 'sashiko review --agent' or 'sashiko-cli local --agent' with a Sashiko server up. The effect is a hung or resource-heavy CLI call, not data loss, money or false output, so Low. On the server path, handle_local posted to /api/submit and returned at once. The review then ran in src/reviewer.rs, where ReviewContext.semaphore (Semaphore::new(settings.review.concurrency)) bounded concurrent reviews, and the tool loop used timeout_at against settings.review.timeout_seconds (default 3600) with child.start_kill() on expiry. With --agent, the new '&& !agent' guard skips that branch, so the review runs in a local worker subprocess. The only bound left is per-process: run_worker_in_worktree buffers patches with buffer_unordered(concurrency) and caps model calls with its own llm_semaphore. Nothing bounds concurrency across processes, so N parallel agent invocations give N times the worktrees and model calls, and the shared server limit no longer applies. The wait is 'child.wait_with_output().await' with no tokio::time::timeout. The only deadline inside the worker is DeadlineBudget, which stops backoff retries and is not a kill switch. A provider call that stalls (api_timeout_secs defaults to 300 per HTTP call; stdio or cli providers may have no such bound, which I could not verify) keeps the caller blocked, and an agent loop has no wall-clock cutoff. kill_on_drop(true) only helps if the caller is cancelled. The missing timeout is preexisting for --force-local and for the no-server cold start, so the new part is that --agent makes it the default even when a server with limits is running. The commit message states the bypass is intentional for determinism, so this is a hardening gap. To confirm severity, check whether the stdio/claude-cli providers can hang without their own timeout. A fix would be wrapping wait_with_output in tokio::time::timeout(settings.review.timeout_seconds) with an explicit kill, or at least documenting that --agent has no limit.

locations.code_snippet:
let output = child
    .wait_with_output()
    .await
    .context("Failed to wait for review subprocess")?;
locations.why_this_location_matters: The worker wait has no wall-clock timeout, and --agent now always takes this path instead of the server queue.
This guard routes agent runs around the /api/submit queue, where reviewer.rs applies the review semaphore and timeout_seconds kill.

dismissed_concerns_DO_NOT_COUNT.description: test_skip_report_skips_report_and_summary_stages uses stages Some(goal), so manual stages may already keep the report and summary stages from running. That would make the mock bail guard and the summary assertion vacuous, and the test would stay green if both skip_if(|s| s.skip_report) calls were removed.
dismissed_concerns_DO_NOT_COUNT.reasoning: 1. manual_stages only gates three things: the pre-screen stage, the planning stage and the analysis stage list. In both workflows `.skip_if(|s| s.manual_stages.is_some())` appears only on prescreen_stage and planning_stage. `resolve_analysis_stages_with_options` uses manual_stages only to choose which analysis stages run. 2. The workflow builders add report_stage unconditionally. The Sashiko builder also adds summary_stage unconditionally: `.stage(report_stage(max_turns, temperature))` and `.stage(summary_stage(max_turns, temperature))`. The Linux builder adds `.stage(report_stage(max_turns, temperature))` after the findings early-exit. No manual_stages condition touches them, so Some(goal) does not suppress them. 3. Without skip_report, the only remaining skip is `s.findings.is_empty()` on the Sashiko report stage. The test mock returns a verification finding, so findings has one entry. The report stage therefore runs in Sashiko. The summary stage has no other skip condition and also runs. For Linux, the early_exit_if checks are all passed because the mock returns concerns and then a finding, so report_stage runs. 4. The mock fails on exactly those prompts. The Linux report prompt ends with 'Return raw text output, not JSON.', which the mock matches. The Sashiko report and summary prompts begin '# Generate plain-text inline review report' and '# Summarize the proposed change'. Each matches a `bail!("report or summary stage should have been skipped")`, and `worker.run(...).expect("worker should succeed")` would then fail. 5. The mock's verification, goal, dedup and conflict-resolution branches match both projects' headings (for example '# Verify remaining concerns and calibrate severity' for Sashiko), so the pipeline reaches the report stage before the assertions. 6. Removing the Linux report skip_if or the Sashiko report or summary skip_if therefore makes the test fail, and the loop covers both ProjectId::Linux and ProjectId::Sashiko. A control run with skip_report false is not needed to show this; the stage ordering and the bail guard show it. Minor note, not a finding: the `summary == ""` assertion is trivially true for Linux because Linux has no summary stage, but the bail guard and review_inline assertion still exercise the Linux skip.

locations.why_this_location_matters: Report and summary stages are added unconditionally; manual_stages does not remove them, so the test reaches them.
This is the only skip condition on the summary stage; removing it makes the summary prompt reach the mock's bail guard and fail the test.
This is the only skip on the Linux report stage, and findings are non-empty in the test, so removal triggers the 'Return raw text output, not JSON.' bail.
Manual stages only replace the analysis stage list and skip prescreen and planning; the test still reaches report and summary, so the skip assertions are not vacuous.

B.summary:
This change adds an --agent flag to "sashiko review" and "sashiko-cli
local" so AI coding agents get compact, non-interactive, machine-readable
output from local reviews. In agent mode the report and summary LLM stages
are skipped, prompts and server submission are bypassed, and a concise JSON
object is printed.

Before:
  sashiko review --project sashiko HEAD~1..HEAD printed either the human
  report (--format text) or the full JSON (--format json), including raw
  LLM history, input_context, dismissed concerns and inline_review. The
  report and summary stages always ran when findings existed. A dirty
  worktree on a terminal prompted "Do you want to proceed? [y/N]", and
  "sashiko-cli local" submitted to a running server if one was reachable.

After:
  sashiko review --project sashiko --agent HEAD~1..HEAD runs the same
  analysis and verification stages but skips the report and summary
  stages, never prompts about a dirty worktree, and prints JSON such as:

  {"status": "issues_found", "baseline": "abc1234", "patches": [...],
   "findings": [...], "concerns": [...], "tokens_in": 1200,
   "tokens_out": 300, "tokens_cached": 800}

  Status is "error" if the result carries an error, "issues_found" if
  there are findings, otherwise "clean". When present, "partial" and a
  non-null "error" are included. History, input_context, inline_review
  and dismissed_concerns are omitted. The --format option is ignored when
  --agent is set. "sashiko-cli local --agent" always runs the review
  locally instead of via the server, forwards --agent to the worker, and
  skips the interactive pause-and-rerun loop.

GEMINI.md now tells agents to pass --agent in the local review loop.

Internally, the flag is threaded through ReviewOptions, WorkerOptions,
WorkerConfig and the workflow state as skip_report. The report and summary
stages in the Linux and Sashiko patch-review workflows are skipped when it
is set, and a new format_agent_review_output function builds the compact
payload. Tests cover flag parsing, the output formatter for clean, issues
and error cases, and a worker run confirming the report and summary stages
are not invoked.
B.inline_review:
- [MEDIUM] In src/local_review.rs (format_agent_review_output and
  run_worker_in_worktree), --agent reports status clean when no AI review
  ran. With --agent --no-ai, which both CLIs accept together, the worker
  clears patches_to_review and returns review: null with no error key and
  zero tokens. The same early return is taken when review_patch_index
  matches no patch. The formatter turns the missing review into empty
  findings and no error, so status is clean. An agent following GEMINI.md
  cannot tell this from a real clean review. The new test has no review:
  null case, so it would not fail on this defect. Emit a distinct status
  (not_reviewed or error) and add a test.

- [MEDIUM] In src/main.rs (handle_review_command) and src/bin/sashiko-cli.rs
  (handle_local), --agent emits no JSON when the review fails outright.
  The early return from result? skips the agent branch, so failures in
  run_git_review (worktree creation, baseline resolution, a patch that
  fails to apply) and the "Review subprocess produced no output" and parse
  failures in handle_local print nothing on stdout. Only soft failures
  produce the status error JSON. The commit message promises error
  metadata in the JSON object. A consumer that parses only stdout sees an
  empty stream, a second undocumented error shape. The exit code is
  non-zero, which limits the damage.

- [MEDIUM] In src/local_review.rs (review_single_patch,
  run_worker_in_worktree) and src/bin/sashiko-cli.rs (handle_local), the
  new --agent branches have no test. The risky one is review_single_patch
  bypassing extract_inline_review when options.agent is set. If that guard

  something to report. The inline_review blanking, the dirty-prompt bypass,

  unexercised. The Worker test sets skip_report directly and does not go

- [LOW] In src/local_review.rs (format_agent_review_output) and src/main.rs
  (handle_review_command), the --agent status and the exit code disagree
  and no document says which one gates. Status is issues_found for any
  finding, including preexisting, Low and Medium ones. The exit code is 1
  only for new High or Critical findings, so a run can print issues_found
  and exit 0. A loop that stops on status clean may never converge on
  preexisting findings, while a loop that gates on the exit code treats
  new Medium findings as done. GEMINI.md only says to resolve reported
  issues. The exit-code policy is inherited, but the status field is new.
  Each finding carries severity and preexisting, so a careful consumer
  can compute the gate itself.

- [LOW] In src/bin/sashiko-cli.rs (handle_local and Commands::Local),
  --agent silently overrides --interactive, --format and the server
  queue. interactive && !agent drops the rebuttal re-run with no message,
  the agent branch ignores --format, and !force_local && !agent skips a
  running server without saying the review ran locally. clap declares no
  conflicts_with and the help text mentions none of this. The commit
  message states only the server bypass. The effect is limited to callers
  that combine flags.

- [LOW] In src/main.rs (handle_review_command), --agent skips the
  dirty-worktree confirmation prompt, and the output JSON has no field
  showing the review ran over uncommitted changes. Findings may describe
  code that is not in the commit under review, and the consuming agent

  reading stdout does not see it.

findings.problem: --agent emits no JSON when the review fails outright
findings.explanation: An agent that parses stdout gets an empty stream plus a stderr message on the worst failures, and only gets the status:error JSON for soft failures. In handle_review_command, `let result = result?;` returns before the new `if agent` branch, so run_git_review failures (worktree creation, baseline resolution, a patch that fails to apply) print nothing on stdout. handle_local has the same early return for 'Review subprocess produced no output' and for parse failures. The commit message promises a JSON object with any error metadata, and the only test feeds a hand-built Value to the formatter. Consumers must treat empty stdout plus a non-zero exit as a second, undocumented error shape. A loop that only parses stdout can read this as nothing to fix. The exit code is non-zero, which limits the damage.

findings.problem: --agent reports status clean when no AI review ran
findings.explanation: A machine consumer is told clean when nothing was reviewed. Reachable today with sashiko review --agent --no-ai, which both CLIs accept together: handle_local and handle_review_command in the diff add no rejection or override of --agent with --no-ai. In run_worker_in_worktree, options.no_ai clears patches_to_review. If all patches applied, the patches_to_review.is_empty() branch returns review: null with no error key and zero tokens. The same branch is taken whenever review_patch_index matches no patch or the patch list is empty (for example an empty commit range); I did not trace whether an earlier stage rejects an empty range, so that trigger is an assumption. format_agent_review_output then turns the missing review into empty findings and concerns through unwrap_or_default. result_has_error is false because there is no error string, so status is clean. GEMINI.md tells agents to run sashiko review --project sashiko --agent and resolve reported issues, so an agent has no signal in the payload to distinguish this from a real clean review. The human path may distinguish the no-review case; I did not verify print_review_result. Partly refuted parts of the candidate: when any patch fails to apply, the worker returns error 'Patch application failed', so status is error. When a per-patch review fails, the aggregate result sets partial and error via combined_review_error, so status is error. Those shapes are handled. The new test covers only a review object with empty findings, an issues result, and an error result. It has no review: null case, so it would not fail on this defect. Capped at Medium because the --no-ai trigger requires an explicit flag combination and the empty-range trigger is unverified. A fix is to emit a distinct status such as not_reviewed (or error) when review is null, and to add a test for it.

findings.problem: --agent status and exit code disagree and no doc says which gates
findings.explanation: Consequence: an agent in the local review loop can get contradictory pass/fail signals. Reachability: every `sashiko review --agent` and `sashiko-cli local --agent` run that has findings, which GEMINI.md makes the required pre-PR step. In format_agent_review_output, `status` is "issues_found" whenever `findings` is non-empty, including preexisting, Low and Medium findings. In handle_review_command (src/main.rs), the exit code is 3 on error and 1 only when result_has_high_or_critical_findings is true, meaning a new (non-preexisting) High or Critical finding. Otherwise it is 0. So a run with only preexisting or Medium/Low findings prints status issues_found and exits 0. A loop that stops on status == clean may never converge when the findings are preexisting, because the agent cannot fix them in the patch under review. A loop that gates on exit 0 treats new Medium findings as done. Verification: GEMINI.md (line 12 and the Stage 1 bullet) says only to 'resolve any reported issues' and 're-verify until ... the local self-review pass[es] cleanly'. It does not name `status` or the exit code as the gate, and docs/ has no mention of --agent or issues_found. The exit-code policy was already there for human mode, so the divergence itself is inherited. What is new is the `status` field, which gives the agent a second, stricter signal with no documented precedence. The new test test_format_agent_review_output_clean_and_issues_and_error covers status only, and nothing pins its relationship to the exit code. Mitigation: each finding carries its own `severity` and `preexisting` fields, so a careful consumer can compute the gate itself. That is why this is Low rather than Medium. It is also an unverified-assumption finding about how the agent consumes the output. Confirming evidence would be an agent loop that branches on `status` alone.

locations.why_this_location_matters: Any finding, including preexisting, Low or Medium, sets status to issues_found.
The exit code uses a stricter predicate (new High or Critical only), so it can be 0 while status is issues_found.

C.summary:
This change adds an --agent flag to sashiko review and sashiko-cli local.
It gives AI coding agents a small, deterministic, non-interactive JSON
result instead of the human report plus bulky LLM history. In agent mode
the report and summary stages are skipped, which saves an LLM round-trip,
and GEMINI.md now tells agents to pass --agent.

Before:
  sashiko review --project sashiko HEAD prints a human-formatted report.
  With --format json it prints the full result, including history,
  input_context, inline_review and dismissed concerns. On a terminal, a
  dirty worktree prompts "Do you want to proceed? [y/N]". sashiko-cli
  local submits to a running server if one is reachable. The report and
  summary LLM stages always run when findings exist.

After:
  sashiko review --project sashiko --agent HEAD prints one JSON object:
    {"status": "clean" | "issues_found" | "error",
     "baseline": "...", "patches": [...], "findings": [...],
     "concerns": [...], "tokens_in": N, "tokens_out": N,
     "tokens_cached": N}
  The keys "partial" and "error" are added when present. History,
  input_context, inline_review and dismissed concerns are omitted. No
  dirty-worktree prompt appears. sashiko-cli local never goes through the
  server, and its interactive re-run loop is disabled. The report and
  summary stages are skipped, so review_inline and summary come back as
  empty strings, and the planned-stage progress list drops "report" and
  "summary".

Internally, the flag is threaded through ReviewOptions, WorkerOptions, the
hidden worker subcommand and WorkerConfig as skip_report. It is applied as
a skip_if condition on the report and summary stages of both the Linux and
Sashiko patch-review workflows. A new format_agent_review_output function
builds the concise payload, and tests cover CLI parsing, the formatter and
the skipped stages in the worker.
C.inline_review:
- [MEDIUM] In src/main.rs (handle_review_command) and
  src/bin/sashiko-cli.rs (handle_local), --agent prints no JSON on a hard
  failure. The error return on the review result comes before the agent
  output branch, so a failed run leaves stdout empty. It exits 1, the same
  code used for new high or critical findings, so a crashed review and a
  blocking finding look alike unless stderr is parsed. This contradicts the
  commit message, which promises error metadata in the JSON.

- [MEDIUM] In src/local_review.rs (format_agent_review_output), status falls
  back to clean when no review ran. With --no-ai, an empty patch list, or a
  review-patch-index that matches no patch, run_worker_in_worktree returns
  early with review null and no error key. The formatter turns the missing
  findings into an empty list and reports clean. GEMINI.md makes this status
  the gate before opening a PR, so an unreviewed change is reported as
  clean. Add a distinct status such as not_reviewed. The unit test covers
  only well-formed inputs and would pass with this bug present.

- [LOW] In src/bin/sashiko-cli.rs (handle_local) and src/main.rs
  (handle_review_command), --agent silently overrides other options. It
  drops --interactive and ignores --format with no message, and it skips a
  running daemon, while docs/sashiko-cli.md neither lists --agent nor says
  so. The dirty-tree prompt is skipped and the warning goes only to stderr,
  and the agent JSON has no dirty field, so a stdout-only reader cannot tell
  that uncommitted changes were reviewed. Print a stderr note for the
  overridden flags, add a dirty field, and document --agent.

- [LOW] In src/worker/prompts.rs (Worker::run, ParallelResolved handler),
  the new filter that removes report and summary from planned_stages is not
  exercised by any test. The only skip_report test, test_skip_report_skips_
  report_and_summary_stages, passes None as the progress callback, so the
  ReviewStarted event is never built. The Linux iteration has no summary
  stage, so its summary assertion is trivially true. With --agent the
  progress total could include stages that never start. Add a test that
  passes a callback and checks planned_stages.

- [LOW] In src/bin/sashiko-cli.rs (handle_local, find_worker_command), the
  --agent flag is forwarded to a worker binary chosen only because the file
  exists, with no version check. A stale sashiko next to sashiko-cli, in the
  parent directory, or on PATH rejects --agent as an unknown argument, and
  the local review fails with a clap usage error and no hint of version
  skew. Add a version handshake or a clear rebuild error.

findings.problem: --agent emits no JSON on hard failure, exits like findings
findings.explanation: A review that never produced a result prints nothing to stdout in --agent mode, and a caller driving the loop from GEMINI.md cannot read a status from it. In handle_review_command the `let result = result?;` line sits before the `if agent` branch (visible in the diff), so any run_git_review Err (bad range, worktree or provider failure) propagates out of main with an empty stdout. A main that returns Err exits 1, which is the same code used for new high/critical findings, so a crashed review and a blocking finding look the same unless stderr is parsed. handle_local has the same shape: an empty or unparseable worker stdout returns Err before the agent branch. The commit message promises JSON with 'any error or partial-completion metadata', but that holds only when the worker returned a result object. I rate it Medium because the failure is loud on stderr and in the exit code, not hidden, and the agent can still react to it. The handle_local half and the exit-code collision rely on code outside the diff.

locations.why_this_location_matters: The error return precedes the agent JSON, so no machine-readable error object is emitted.
Subprocess failure bypasses format_agent_review_output.

findings.problem: --agent reports status clean when no review ran (--no-ai, empty set)
findings.explanation: A change that was never reviewed is reported as clean, and GEMINI.md makes that status the gate before opening a PR. Reachable now by passing --agent together with --no-ai (both parse, and the diff's own parser test combines them), by an empty patch list, or by a --review-patch-index that matches no patch. Proof: run_worker_in_worktree clears patches_to_review when options.no_ai is set. All patches then apply, so the !all_applied branch is skipped. The patches_to_review.is_empty() branch returns early with review null, tokens 0, and no error and no partial key. format_agent_review_output reads review.findings through and_then/unwrap_or_default, so findings becomes an empty vec. result_has_error is false because there is no error key. The status chain then falls through to the final else and yields clean. The output is identical to a real clean review apart from zero token counters, and no status value such as skipped or not_reviewed exists. This is the unwrap_or_default-to-success shape from silent-failure.md. Severity is Medium rather than High because I did not confirm that an empty range reaches this branch instead of failing earlier in input resolution, and the --no-ai combination is an explicit operator choice. The fix is to treat a null or missing review as a distinct status (not_reviewed, or error), and to cover it in test_format_agent_review_output_clean_and_issues_and_error, which only exercises well-formed clean, issues and error inputs and would pass with the bug present.

locations.why_this_location_matters: The only place the verdict is computed. The fallback is clean, and a missing or null review collapses to empty findings.
--no-ai clears patches_to_review, so the early return with review null is taken with no error key.
The early return emits review null, zero tokens and no error or partial, which the formatter maps to clean.

findings.explanation: Consequence: an agent or user who passes --agent together with --interactive, --format text or a running daemon gets different behaviour than the flags promise, with no message, and the JSON cannot tell the reader that the reviewed tree was dirty. Reachability: every 'sashiko review --agent' and 'sashiko-cli local --agent' call. GEMINI.md now tells agents to use this on every PR. Confirmed in the diff: (1) In handle_local, 'if interactive && !agent && (has_error || has_issues)' turns --interactive into a single run with no stderr note, and the output branch 'if agent' never reads 'format'. (2) The daemon check is now '!force_local && !agent', so --agent never submits to a running daemon, but docs/sashiko-cli.md:182-185 still says local delegates to a running daemon unless --force-local is passed, and the flags table at lines 178-179 lacks --agent. The doc reads as if --agent will use the daemon, which it does not. (3) In handle_review_command (src/main.rs:2038-2046) the dirty-tree warning goes only to stderr and the y/N prompt is skipped when agent is set. format_agent_review_output (src/local_review.rs) emits status, baseline, patches, findings, concerns and tokens, with no dirty field, so a stdout-only consumer sees status 'clean' or 'issues_found' for a tree that included uncommitted changes. is_dirty(...).unwrap_or(false) also treats a failed dirty check as clean (preexisting). The prompt was already TTY-only, so the change matters only for terminal-run agents, and the stderr warning remains, which is why this stays Low. Unverified and not reported as a bug: contention with a running daemon on the same repo. Local runs create their own GitWorktree (src/local_review.rs:402) and concurrency semaphore, the same path --force-local already uses. Confirming this would need a read of GitWorktree::new naming and the daemon's worktree dir. Suggested fix: add a 'dirty' boolean to the agent JSON, print a stderr note when --agent is combined with --interactive, and document --agent in docs/sashiko-cli.md.

The dirty-tree confirmation is skipped under --agent and the warning goes only to stderr.

findings.problem: skip_report progress filter in Worker::run has no test
findings.explanation: Only the review progress display is affected, and the failure is cosmetic: with --agent the progress bar total could include report and summary stages that never start, so the bar stops short. It is reachable only when a progress callback is passed (the sashiko review CLI path). The candidate's main claim, that the worker test passes vacuously, is mostly not proven. Evidence: (1) Sashiko CONSOLIDATION_STAGES includes REPORT and SUMMARY, and the report stage has skip_if(skip_report || findings.is_empty()). The mock returns one High finding, so without skip_report the report stage would run, hit the 'Return raw text output' or '# Generate plain-text inline review report' marker and bail. (2) Stage::execute_isolated checks skip_if before calling the provider. (3) Worker::run propagates stage errors through WorkflowEngine::execute(...).await?, so a bail would fail the expect. (4) Reverting the '!self.skip_report' guard turns review_inline into 'No issues found.' and fails the assertion. Weaker points: Linux CONSOLIDATION_STAGES has no summary stage (only DEDUPLICATION, CONFLICT_RESOLUTION, VERIFICATION, REPORT), so the summary == '' assertion is trivially true for Linux. I did not read the Sashiko summary prompt text, so I have not confirmed that '# Summarize the proposed change' matches it; if it does not, reverting the summary skip_if would not fail the test. The real gap: the test passes progress as None, so the event_cb branch 'planned_stages.retain(|s| s != "report" && s != "summary")' never executes. planned_stages_from does return report (both projects) and summary (Sashiko) from CONSOLIDATION_STAGES, so the filter changes real output, and skipped stages never emit StageStarted or StageFinished, which is why the filter is needed. This is new logic that no test executes. Likewise, the server bypass in handle_local and the dirty-worktree prompt bypass in handle_review_command are exercised only by clap parse tests, not behaviour tests. Those are not reported separately. Confirm by adding a test that runs Worker::run with a progress callback and skip_report true, asserting ReviewStarted.planned_stages contains neither report nor summary.

locations.why_this_location_matters: Passing None as the progress argument means the retain filter and ReviewStarted event are never exercised; the Linux iteration also has no summary stage, so the summary assertion is trivial there.

findings.problem: local --agent forwarded to unversioned worker found by directory search
findings.explanation: Consequence: when handle_local runs a stale sashiko worker, the new --agent flag is rejected as an unknown argument, so the local review fails with a clap usage error and no hint of version skew. The failure is loud and recoverable by rebuilding, so it is not silent false output. Reachability: find_worker_command (src/bin/sashiko-cli.rs:2203) never checks that the worker matches the current build. Its search order is: (1) sashiko in the directory of the running sashiko-cli executable, (2) sashiko in that directory's parent, (3) sashiko-review in the same directory with no subcommand, (4) sashiko on PATH via `which`, (5) sashiko-review on PATH via `which`. The first existing file wins on `exists()` alone. The stale-worker case is concrete. Running `cargo build --bin sashiko-cli` or `cargo run --bin sashiko-cli -- local ... --agent` rebuilds only the CLI, so an older target/debug/sashiko sitting next to it is used. The same happens with an installed sashiko-cli beside an older sashiko, or an older sashiko-review fallback, which was never given --agent. handle_local pushes `--agent` onto the worker args (line ~1988) whenever the flag is set, without checking worker capability. Assumption to confirm: I did not read the worker spawn and error handling at lines 1963-2125. If a non-zero worker exit is reported only as a generic failure, the clap message may be lost; otherwise it shows as a clap usage error. A version handshake or a clear 'rebuild sashiko' error would remove the ambiguity. Separate pre-existing issue in the same function, not part of this change: it checks `dir.join("sashiko")` without .exe and uses `which`, which does not exist on Windows, so worker discovery likely fails there.

locations.why_this_location_matters: The first existing binary is chosen on existence alone, so a stale sashiko next to sashiko-cli, in the parent directory, or on PATH can be selected with no version check.
--agent is appended to this worker's args unconditionally, so an older worker rejects it as an unknown flag.

dismissed_concerns_DO_NOT_COUNT.description: --agent might not reach the worker or the workflow stages.
dismissed_concerns_DO_NOT_COUNT.reasoning: The flag is traced end to end: handle_local pushes --agent into the worker args, main.rs passes it into WorkerOptions, which feeds skip_report in WorkerConfig and then the workflow state, and both workflows gate their report stages on skip_report. sashiko review forwards it through ReviewOptions. The daemon-spawned worker leaves it false, so that path is unchanged.

locations.why_this_location_matters: The workflow honours the flag.

dismissed_concerns_DO_NOT_COUNT.description: The worker's stderr pipe might not be drained, so the child could block.
dismissed_concerns_DO_NOT_COUNT.reasoning: stderr is drained line by line in a separate tokio::spawn task, with a bounded 100-line tail, while wait_with_output collects stdout. Both pipes are consumed concurrently, and the change does not touch this path.

locations.why_this_location_matters: stderr is drained concurrently.

dismissed_concerns_DO_NOT_COUNT.description: skip_report might be shared mutable state between the progress callback and the worker.
dismissed_concerns_DO_NOT_COUNT.reasoning: skip_report is a plain bool copied into a local before the move closure, so the closure owns an immutable copy. The workflow state field is set once at construction, and there is no static, lock or atomic.

locations.why_this_location_matters: The flag is captured by value.

dismissed_concerns_DO_NOT_COUNT.description: a patch that failed to apply, a per-patch Worker error, or an incomplete patch review is reported as clean.
dismissed_concerns_DO_NOT_COUNT.reasoning: Each of these sets a top-level error string. A patch-apply failure takes the !all_applied branch, which returns an error of 'Patch application failed' and is checked before the empty-review return, so it is never confused with a skipped review. A per-patch review_single_patch Err is pushed into review_errors after mark_patch_review_incomplete, and the combined result then gets both partial true and error set via combined_review_error. result_has_error is true for a non-empty top-level error string, so the formatter returns status error in those cases. partial is only inserted together with error, so the 'partial with no error' scenario is not reachable from the code read. This dismissal covers only those sub-claims; the no-review path is reported as a finding.

locations.why_this_location_matters: The apply-failure return carries a non-empty error, so the formatter yields error.
Per-patch failures are aggregated and both partial and error are inserted on the top-level result.

dismissed_concerns_DO_NOT_COUNT.description: In agent mode review_single_patch skips extract_inline_review, so a missing or malformed worker output is no longer rejected and retried, and could surface as a clean review.
dismissed_concerns_DO_NOT_COUNT.reasoning: extract_inline_review (src/local_review.rs:504-524) has exactly one Err path: `has_findings && inline_content.is_none()`, meaning findings are present but review_inline is missing or empty. A None output, a non-object output, or a missing findings key makes has_findings false, so the function returns Ok(None). The skipped guard therefore never rejected missing or malformed output in non-agent mode either, and agent mode loses no output-shape check. The only retry trigger lost is 'findings present, inline report empty'. In agent mode that condition is always true when findings exist, because skip_report skips the report stage in both workflows (linux_patch_review.rs and sashiko_patch_review.rs skip_if(|s| s.skip_report)). Keeping the guard would turn every agent run with findings into a failed attempt that is retried until it exhausts its attempts, so bypassing it is required. format_agent_review_output reads only review.findings, review.concerns, baseline, patches, tokens, partial and error, and never inline_review, so nothing downstream depends on the skipped value. Error and partial states come from result_has_error and the error/partial fields, which this change does not touch, so a failed run is still reported as status 'error'. Whether a None worker output surfaces as 'clean' is pre-existing behaviour that this change neither introduces nor worsens.

locations.why_this_location_matters: This is the only Err path in the function. Missing or non-object output yields Ok(None), so the check skipped in agent mode validated nothing beyond the inline-report presence.
The bypass is consistent with the report stage being skipped in agent mode. Keeping the check would fail every agent run that has findings.

dismissed_concerns_DO_NOT_COUNT.description: The agent JSON status is issues_found for any non-empty findings, while the process exit code is 1 only for new high/critical findings and 3 for error, so a consumer could be misled about which signal to trust.
dismissed_concerns_DO_NOT_COUNT.reasoning: 1) The exit-code logic is not conditional on agent. In handle_local, has_error leads to exit(3) and new critical or high findings lead to exit(1) after the agent JSON is printed. In handle_review_command, result_has_error leads to exit(3) and result_has_high_or_critical_findings leads to exit(1). A failed review therefore never exits 0 in agent mode, and the exit-code behaviour is unchanged from before this commit. 2) The status field and the exit code answer different questions. Exit code is a CI-style gate that already existed (new high/critical only). status is the agent-loop signal: GEMINI.md tells agents to 'resolve any reported issues', so any non-empty findings list is correctly issues_found. 3) The error case is consistent between the two signals: format_agent_review_output uses result_has_error(result) for status 'error', the same predicate that drives exit code 3, so the two signals cannot disagree on failure. 4) Consumers can reconcile them without ambiguity. The findings array is passed through verbatim from review.findings (cloned, not stripped), so each finding keeps its own severity and preexisting fields. These are the same fields count_severities and result_has_high_or_critical_findings read to compute the exit code (preexisting defaults to false, i.e. new). A consumer that wants the gating criterion can recompute it from the payload. 5) No silent failure or false success results: an errored review is reported as status error with the error string and exits 3, and findings are never hidden. At most this is a documentation nicety, not a defect with a concrete misbehaving input, and it does not meet the bar for a finding.

locations.why_this_location_matters: Exit codes run after the agent JSON is printed and are not gated on agent, so errors still exit 3 and new high/critical findings still exit 1.
Same exit-code policy in sashiko review, unconditional on agent, using the same result_has_error predicate as the JSON status.
The exit-code criterion reads preexisting and severity from the same finding objects that format_agent_review_output passes through unchanged, so consumers can reconcile status and exit code.

dismissed_concerns_DO_NOT_COUNT.description: The report/summary filter on planned_stages uses hard-coded stage names, while StageFinished counting uses is_counted_stage, so the progress numerator and denominator could disagree.
dismissed_concerns_DO_NOT_COUNT.reasoning: 1) planned_stages_from (src/workflows/mod.rs) returns the filtered analysis stages followed by CONSOLIDATION_STAGES names. For Linux that list is dedup, conflict-resolution, verification, report. For Sashiko it is dedup, conflict-resolution, verification, report, summary. The literal names in the retain call match the registered stage names: REPORT has name "report" in both workflows, and SUMMARY has name "summary" in sashiko_patch_review.rs. Linux has no summary consolidation stage, so the "summary" half of the retain is a harmless no-op there. 2) The change adds .skip_if(|s| s.skip_report) to the report stage in both workflows and to the Sashiko summary stage. In Stage::execute_isolated (src/workflow/stage.rs) the skip_if check returns early, before the StageStarted event and before the StageFinished event are emitted. A skipped stage therefore never produces a StageFinished, and is_counted_stage is never consulted for it. 3) The numerator is completed_stages, incremented only on AiReviewStageFinished in src/main.rs. The denominator in patch_stage_total is p.planned_stages.len() plus preliminary stages while a patch is reviewing, and completed_stages once it is Finished or Failed. With skip_report, report and summary are removed from the denominator and are never counted in the numerator, so the two stay consistent. Without skip_report nothing is removed, which is the previous behaviour. 4) The hard-coded literals are a maintainability coupling to the stage tables, not a runtime mismatch, and they only affect progress display. The transient use of default_stage_count before ParallelResolved still includes report and summary. That predates this change, is replaced as soon as the plan arrives, and only affects the progress bar.

locations.why_this_location_matters: The literals match the registered names (REPORT = "report", SUMMARY = "summary"), and the stages they remove are exactly the ones skipped when skip_report is set.
A skipped stage returns before StageStarted and StageFinished are emitted, so it never increments completed_stages. This agrees with its removal from planned_stages.
This shows which stage names (dedup, conflict-resolution, verification, report, summary) end up in the denominator, and that report and summary are among them.
